Validation selection

Each recipe's selected trial, or its highest-recall trial when none qualified. The winner has the highest recall at its saved threshold among qualified recipes. Intervals come from 1,000 resamples of validation transactions shared by all recipes, so the winner's lead over each recipe is a paired comparison. Frauds cluster on cards, so these row-level intervals are, if anything, too narrow: a lead whose interval includes zero is not a measured difference.

Definitions and limitations

Average precision (AP) is sklearn.metrics.average_precision_score (a step-weighted PR summary, not trapezoidal area); random scores achieve the fraud rate. Recall at top x% is the share of frauds among the x% highest-scored transactions, a fixed review volume; tied boundary scores are split evenly. The review budget is the share of transactions analysts can review: each saved threshold is the lowest score that flags no more than that share of validation transactions, and a model qualifies when it then catches more fraud than reviewing a random sample of the same size. The later evaluation compares frozen models by recall at the budget volume; precision, recall, and alert rate at the saved threshold show how the threshold itself carries over to a new month. ROC-AUC is secondary: with rare fraud it stays high for models of little practical use. Train AP is computed on a fixed sample of up to 200,000 training rows; far above validation AP, it indicates overfitting. Inference timing covers batch scoring on the recorded validation rows, excluding data loading. Validation charts describe the selected model, or the highest-average-precision trial when nothing qualifies; evaluation charts describe frozen models and are not used to retune them.

Limitations: synthetic source data and a synthetic fixed label delay. No statistical significance claim, confidence interval gate, economic cost model, or production readiness claim.
